title: 4D570002-Arctic_Thunder.xiso.iso

arms.A: 62ef8bf0fe with --env HAKUX_TCG424_RANGE=0: whole-page TB invalidation, the pre-flip default, kept as an opt-out by this commit
arms.B: 62ef8bf0fe, no --env: the flipped default, range test plus per-page code bitmap. One apk; the env is the only independent variable.

runs: 4D570002-Arctic_Thunder.xiso.iso, --route arctic-thunder, --seconds 420, --frames-every 20, --device thor, MAX (soak_title.sh's default regimen) and its cool gate, 3 runs per arm interleaved A B A B A B, queued together (the v1 pilot is the pilot: the route reaches the race on both arms, and what it needed is in the reader). 420 s: `mark gameplay` falls ~228 s after soak start and the pause began at +388 s at the earliest in the pilot; running longer only adds paused time. 6 x (420 + 90) s = 51 min.
reader: python3 docs/lanes/tcg424flip/arcticread2.py <result ids>, at the commit that adds this file. It is arcticread.py loaded unchanged with the window's far end closed. Window: `mark gameplay` + 30 s to hi, hi = the earliest of (a) soak start + N, N from run.log's `THERMAL: pause ... began after +N s` (the pause's earliest onset), (b) the first gfps sample >= 45 after mark + 30 s (race over: race gfps on the Thor at MAX reached at most 34 in the four runs on disk; the results and menu screens run at 59-60), (c) `soak end`. No mark = VOID. Per run, over [mark + 30, hi): gfps = median of the hakuX-perf gfps samples; churn% = (jcus + rdus) / vCPU cpu over [tlb68]; di/s, inv/s, slow/s, fs/s from hakuX-pages and [tlb68]; on% = sum cpu / sum dt over [tlb68]; cpf = on% x 10 / gfps; gap = the longest gap between gfps samples, including mark + 30 to the first and the last to hi. Per arm: the median of its three per-run values.
why_this_title: lane.slowtier2 (#462, PR #556) found Arctic Thunder the heaviest code churn of any title in gameplay: 7,300-8,300 invalidations and 37,000-42,000 TBs discarded a second, the vCPU 86-87% on-CPU and the frame guest-side. Blinx, where tbflip424-blinx2.json passed, churns 2.1% of the vCPU; Arctic churns 14%. So this is where the lever should pay, and also where the range test's cost (more stores taking the slow path on pages that keep code) is largest.
baseline_on_disk: arcticread.py, Thor, MAX, A path (whole-page, the only path before this commit), 1-1790547557-titleroutes-979135 (677ae13af8) and 1-1790548502-titleroutes-1531400 (e884ad260e): gfps 21 / 23.0, churn% 14.1 / 13.9, di/s 37,642 / 41,061, inv/s 7,364 / 8,092, slow/s 10,221 / 11,202, on% 87.6 / 87.1, cpf 41.7 / 37.9, m50 89 / 88, ng 109 / 126, rt 0, fatal 0, tail 0.5 / -4.0 s. Saved as docs/lanes/tcg424flip/baseline.out. The route changed between the two (A held from m10 on); the arms here both run the current route.

legs.M0 (instrument): Every run has a `mark gameplay` line, >= 20 gfps samples in the bounded window, xx = 0, and m50 >= 40 (the intro and menus run at the cap; the pilot read 75 and 194, the baselines 88-89). A's [tlb68] lines in the window carry rt=0 only; B's carry rt=1 only (B reading rt=1 with no env is this commit's own check: the default is on). A thermal pause no longer voids a run by itself: the window ends where it may have begun. A run failing M0 is VOID, not zero, and is re-queued once on the same arm. More than one VOID run per arm stops the lane without a verdict.
legs.M1 (the counter moves; the falsifier): Per-arm median churn%: A >= 5.0 and B <= 0.5 x A. Per-arm median di/s: B <= 0.1 x A. FAILS in a world where Arctic gameplay's churn is not the #424 mechanisms (A < 5.0, against 13.9-14.1 on disk), or where the range test does not engage (B's di/s stays near A's: the writes land on the translated bytes themselves, and sparing blocks by range spares nothing).
legs.M2a (lane.local's leg: the vCPU's on-CPU: Per-arm median on%: B <= A - 2.0. FAILS in a world where the vCPU spends what the range test saves on more guest work (then gfps rises and M2b says so) or where the slow stores the bitmap adds cost what the discards did.
legs.M2b (vCPU cost per frame falls): Per-arm median cpf: B <= 0.95 x A. This is the same saving measured per unit of work, so it passes whether the vCPU idles the saving or spends it on frames. FAILS in a world where B's extra slow stores (Blinx B took 32-42k a second where A took ~500) eat the ~14% of vCPU time the discards and TLB resets cost on A.
legs.M4' (must not regress, on gameplay): Per-arm median gfps: B >= A - 1. And no run of either arm crashes or hangs: no `Fatal signal` or `FATAL` line in logcat.txt, and gap <= 15 s (pre-pause gaps on all four runs on disk are <= 4.3 s; the 20-27 s gaps in the pilot's B all came after its pause began, and its emulator kept rendering and logging [tlb68] through them). The frames inside the window are read and must show the race (not a frozen, garbled or menu screen). FAILS in a world where the range test's cost outweighs its saving on this title, or where a spared block was stale code the guest then ran (a hang, a crash or a broken race).
legs.decision: Ship the flip (mark PR ready, Closes #424) iff M0, M1 and M4' pass here AND the pgraph must-not-move arm (tcg424flip-pgraph.json) is byte-identical with no unreadable capture. M2a/M2b are the mechanism legs: they decide what the release note may claim, not whether the flip ships (the Blinx rule shipped on M4', and a flip that costs nothing and churns nothing is still correct). If M4' fails, do not ship: report fs/s, inv/s and slow/s per run on #424. If M1 fails, report that Arctic cannot price the lever and do not claim it.

what_this_cannot_see: A gfps change smaller than the run-to-run spread: the two A runs on disk read 21 and 23, on different builds and route revisions, so a true loss under ~2 gfps can pass. Self-modifying code a spared block should have caught but that happens not to show in one race on one track. The Nova (the lever is Thor-measured here). Titles whose writes land on the translated bytes themselves. A race that ends early in B because of stale code, if its end looks like an ordinary finish or time-up: the frames show the screen, not why it came. Anything after the pause's earliest onset.
expect_note: EMPTY ON PURPOSE: a soak writes no captures, so there is no golden key. The legs are read with arcticread.py off the [tlb68], hakuX-pages and hakuX-perf lines. The pixel leg is tcg424flip-pgraph.json.
supersedes: tcg424flip-arctic.json. Its pilot (A 1-1790660189-lane.tcg424flip-1147138, B 1-1790660193-lane.tcg424flip-1148129) is VOID under its own M0: both runs hit the Thor's thermal pause (A began after +451 s, B after +388 s of the 560 s soak). Reading it also showed the open window counts non-race screens: B's race gave way at mark + 100 s to a 59-60 gfps screen with Df:0, a load and a second race, and both titleroutes baselines end their race at mark + 124-161 s the same way. This file changes the window, the soak length, the frames and the hang check. It changes no threshold. Its reader was written after reading the pilot, so the pilot counts toward neither file: it is judged on three fresh pairs.
